text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED - prod-serving cluster node gke-ssd-07 high ephemeral disk usage (90%). Multiple pod evictions observed. Investigating.

alex: saw the page, jumping in. which pods are getting OOM/crashed?

maria: model-runtime pods on node gke-ssd-07. logs show repeated "failed to write checkpoint" and CUDA init errors after restarts.

raj: node is reporting heavy /var/lib/modelcache and /tmp write churn. du shows a few 100s of GB in modelcache and rotated logs.

sarah: customer_success here — customers are seeing elevated 500s and increased latency for streaming responses. I have a small set of tenant IDs; want to confirm impact window.

alex: ok priority: 1) limit further evictions 2) stabilize runtime 3) mitigation for customers. I'm going to cordon the node and start draining low-priority pods.

raj: agree. cordon + selective drain. running:
```
kubectl cordon gke-ssd-07
kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=gke-ssd-07 -o wide
```

maria: don't drain model-runtime pods aggressively — they have local modelcache files. We'll lose warming. Suggest moving ephemeral storage heavy jobs first (batch, log-forwarders).

alex: good point. I'll identify the top disk users and kill the log-forwarder DaemonSet instance on that node first.

alex: doing:
```
kubectl exec -it log-forwarder-77 -- sh -c "du -sh /var/log/* | sort -h | tail -n 20"
rm -rf /var/log/old-app-logs/*
```

raj: we should also trim the modelcache on that node. maria: can runtime tolerate deleting stale caches? any safe cleanup path?

maria: yes, we can evict older model shards for now. Command on node:
```
sudo du -sh /var/lib/modelcache/*
sudo rm -rf /var/lib/modelcache/models/*/shard_old_*
```
But be careful — removes will cause some cold starts.

alex: performed selective rm on biggest log dirs — freed ~120GB. Node disk dropped to ~65%.

incident-bot: Pager: oncall-escalation -> @maria @alex @raj @sarah

sarah: notified customer success and posting a brief: "We're investigating increased errors & latency due to node disk pressure leading to pod restarts. Engineers are mitigating, will update in 30m." 

maria: observed runtime container crash logs showing: "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS during cuInit" after the container restarts repeatedly. Likely related to abrupt eviction and corrupted driver state.

raj: when pods were force-killed, kubelet left some container runtime state and device nodes in weird state. I'm going to rotate the GPU driver on that node and restart kubelet.

alex: status update: cordoned node, evicted low-priority pods, freed disk space, but model-runtime pods are still flapping due to container crashes -> pod restart loop.

maria: workplan:
- restart nvidia-driver + kubelet on gke-ssd-07
- move a subset of model-serving pods to a healthy node pool (temp routing)
- throttle logging to avoid writeback thrash
- apply ephemeral storage quota on model-runtime to prevent full-disk again

alex: executing restart sequence now. running:
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-drm.service nvidia-persistenced
sudo systemctl restart kubelet
```

raj: I'll provision a temporary node with more ephemeral SSD and label it 'spill-over=ephemeral' and increase autoscaler to add 2 nodes.

raj: created node pool tmp-ssd-1, labelled, and increased deployment affinity for emergency. Triggering rollout of small percentage there.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: 10% of model-runtime pods scheduled to node pool tmp-ssd-1

maria: routing changed to send new sessions to tmp-ssd-1 and healthy nodes. Old sessions may still reconnect to restored nodes.

sarah: customer update prepared: "We've mitigated the immediate storage pressure and are routing traffic to healthy nodes. Some customers may see a brief quality/regeneration impact; we expect wrap up in ~45-60 minutes." Sending now.

alex: after driver restart, we still see a few pods logging CUDA init failures; I manually deleted the worst offenders to force reschedule onto healthy nodes. Should restore.

maria: added an ephemeral-storage quota to the k8s deployment:
```
resources:
  requests:
    ephemeral-storage: "1Gi"
  limits:
    ephemeral-storage: "20Gi"
```
This will prevent runaway caches from filling disks in the future.

raj: also enabled logrotate policy for log-forwarder on node to keep daily logs compressed and max 100M per file.

alex: monitoring metrics: disk usage stabilized. pod restarts decreasing. error rate back down to ~2% above baseline (was +12% at peak).

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE - node gke-ssd-07 disk pressure mitigated. paging level -> monitoring. oncall shift: @alex remains primary, @raj supports infra, @maria for runtime.

sarah: Customer success posted an update to affected tenants. No customer data exposure. Will follow-up with RCA once fully stable.

maria: follow-ups for postmortem:
- why modelcache grew unbounded (old shard retention policy)
- surface alerts earlier: ephemeral-storage per-node threshold + modelcache growth anomaly
- add automated eviction script for stale shards when node free < 20%
- QA the driver restart flow during evictions (CUDA fallout)

raj: infra follow-ups:
- ensure node autoscaler can spin tmp-ssd pool faster
- consider limiting local write IO bandwidth for modelcache jobs

alex: summary for ops channel (copying): "Root cause: runaway model cache + rotated logs filled node ephemeral SSD. Resulted in kubelet evictions and container restarts; CUDA driver state corrupted on some restarts causing init errors. Mitigations: freed logs/cache, cordon/drain, restarted drivers/kubelet, created temporary nodes and routed traffic, applied ephemeral-storage quotas and logrotate. Impact: 30-50 minutes, elevated errors and latency for a subset of customers, no data loss. Postmortem items assigned."

sarah: closing customer-facing update thread. Customers appreciate timely updates.

alex: moving incident to monitoring, keeping this thread open for the next 2 hours for any flaps. Great teamwork. :clap:

maria: noted owners for follow-ups: maria -> runtime pruning, raj -> infra autoscaler/IO, alex -> alerting & runbook.

oncall-bot: oncall handoff scheduled at 3187663600. Current primary: alex. Next: tbd.

alex: thanks all. I'll file the postmortem after we gather logs and alloc timeline.
